clue.text: Crooner cradles very, very young chick on bended knee

indicators.note: to cradle is to hold something in your arms, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: Bing Crosby, the most famous crooner
a chick so young it has not yet hatched

explanation.surface: A singer gently holding a newborn bird while kneeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very, very young' pushes the chick back before hatching. Bing Crosby is the classic crooner of crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pleading earnestly is figuratively down on their knees, so the idiom describes an act of entreaty.

clue.text: Loss of nude confronts that Spanish cubist

blocks.note: a nude has lost her clothes, a bra among them
que is Spanish for 'that'

explanation.surface: A Spanish cubist painter faces the loss of a nude from his work.
explanation.walkthrough: Many solvers thought 'Loss of nude' a stretch: the garment is what a nude has lost. 'Spanish' misleads, since Georges BRAQUE was French; Picasso was the Spanish cubist.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Braque co-founded the Cubist movement in painting alongside Picasso.

clue.text: Animal heard with a song, to be reasonable?

indicators.note: something heard is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.clueFragment: with a song, to be reasonable
blocks.note: to go for a song is to sell cheaply, at a reasonable price

explanation.surface: A creature that can be heard singing, asking whether it is reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go for a song' is the idiom for selling very cheaply; the two words 'go for' sound like the burrowing rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: A gopher is a burrowing rodent of North America, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Weakness shown by patriarchal seat of old empire?

blocks.note: the Inca empire of ancient Peru
a pa is a father, the patriarch of a family
a seat of government or power is a city

explanation.surface: A weakness revealed by the patriarch's throne in a fallen empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' reverses the order, so the empire comes first; the clue also reads as the father placed inside the empire's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Incapacity is a lack of strength or ability, so it is a synonym of weakness.

clue.text: Adding to visage nicely, referring to make-up?

indicators.note: the letters wanted go to make up part of the following words, adding to them from within

blocks.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Cosmetics that improve a face nicely: is that what make-up means?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' suggests cosmetics, but the definition means genetic make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Genic means relating to genes, which determine an organism's genetic constitution or inherited composition.

clue.text: Farmer detailing bearer of small vegetarian gifts?

indicators.note: de-tailing means cutting off the tail, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a Santa bringing a pea, a small vegetable gift

explanation.surface: A farmer itemising who brings little meat-free presents.
explanation.walkthrough: A whimsical 'pea Santa' brings tiny vegetable gifts; cut its last letter to leave PEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a poor smallholder or agricultural labourer, so a type of farmer.

clue.text: China or Chile on the outside breaking clear

indicators.note: only the outer letters of the country are wanted
breaking into something means entering its middle, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: taken as written
first and last letters
clear and plain both mean obvious

explanation.surface: Two countries, China or Chile, seen from outside as something breaks clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like a country to pair with Chile, but it means fine crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: China is the everyday name for fine ceramic tableware, which is porcelain.

clue.text: Long facial hair, bald on top

indicators.note: a bald head has lost its top, so the first letter is removed

blocks.note: tache is British slang for a moustache

explanation.surface: A long moustache on a man whose head is bald.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' reads as an adjective for the hair but is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to yearn for it, so ache and long are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: Little taste in an elephant's tusks, might you say?

indicators.note: asks how the phrase would come out when spoken, sound over spelling

blocks.note: tusks are a pair of overgrown teeth

explanation.surface: A tiny taste found on an elephant's ivory.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'a pair o' teeth' runs together into the French word for a pre-dinner drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is a small alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Transported cases fully made

indicators.note: to case something is to enclose it, as in a box

blocks.note: toted means carried
all, as in 'all done', means fully

explanation.surface: Packing cases have been carried and fully assembled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' is meant as in 'two and two made four'.
explanation.definitionFit: Totalled means amounted to, as a sum makes a figure, so it fits made in arithmetic.

clue.text: Jelly equally good with custard or cream, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: as in 'as good as'
pi is short for pious, so good
both words begin with the same letter

explanation.surface: A dessert jelly tastes just as good with custard or with cream.
explanation.walkthrough: The pudding picture misleads: this is the savoury meat jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to glaze or set cold dishes.

clue.text: Point thrown out?

blocks.note: surface reading: an argument dismissed in debate
setter's reading: a compass point whose letters include a jumble of the word thrown

explanation.walkthrough: Commenters argued over the exact parse: the answer contains the letters of THROWN mixed up, with the question mark hinting at the device rather than a full wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Northwest is one of the intermediate compass points, halfway between north and west.

clue.text: Sudden twists due, next bandaging muscle

indicators.note: twisting something turns it round, so the letters get rearranged
a bandage wraps round a limb, so these letters go round another piece

blocks.note: the fodder
pec is short for pectoral muscle

explanation.surface: Sudden twists of a muscle are due, followed by bandaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unexpected comes without warning, so it is abrupt or sudden.

clue.text: Charge speechifying Liz's fella, commonly?

indicators.note: making a speech means the word is taken as spoken

blocks.note: Prince Philip, husband of Queen Elizabeth, informally called Phil

explanation.surface: A charge of speechmaking against the late Queen's husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Liz is Queen Elizabeth II; her husband was Prince Philip.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a glass or a gun is to load or fill it.

clue.text: Got trousers on? Lie! One lacking – if so?

definitions.text: Got trousers on? Lie! One lacking – if so?

indicators.note: lacking means missing, so a letter for one is dropped
used as a verb, to trouser something is to pocket it, so it is held inside

blocks.note: bagged means obtained
re means on, concerning
taken as written
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be wearing trousers; it is a lie, and the person without them has bare legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' is a verb meaning pockets: BAGGED holds RE plus LIE without I.
explanation.definitionFit: If you are lying about wearing trousers, your legs are uncovered, which is the whole clue's picture of being barelegged.

clue.text: A tramp I trained, inspired by old fellow, qualified

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the letters are rearranged
to be inspired is to be breathed in, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: cove is old slang for a man
the fodder

explanation.surface: A vagrant I coached, motivated by an elderly man, passed his exams.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative means relative, holding only by comparison, so a qualified rather than absolute statement.

clue.text: Piece covering biscuit – bourbon might be in it

blocks.note: a piece in chess or draughts is a man
a head covering
biscuit is a pale brown colour

explanation.surface: A slice of chocolate topping a biscuit, perhaps a Bourbon one.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bourbon is a British chocolate sandwich biscuit, so 'biscuit' and 'bourbon' both seem to be about snacks; here bourbon is whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manhattan is a cocktail made with whiskey, often bourbon, plus vermouth and bitters.

clue.text: Cold and calculating people in on event

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
C for cold, as on a tap
Casio, the electronics firm famous for calculators

explanation.surface: Cold, scheming types are in on the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold and calculating' reads as a description of people; it is C plus a calculator maker.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasion is a particular event or happening, especially a special one.

clue.text: Adventure tours always most odd

indicators.note: to tour is to travel around, so these letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: a quest is an adventurous journey
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: Adventure holidays are always the strangest.
explanation.definitionFit: Queer in its older sense means strange, so the superlative means strangest.

clue.text: Tolerate mug

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to permit or approve
second meaning: mug is slang for face

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup or a dupe; it is the slang for a face.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning allow or support and a noun meaning a face or expression.

clue.text: Alas, I lament losing leader of a US state

indicators.note: losing its leader means the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: an exclamation of regret
taken as written
to moan is to lament

explanation.surface: Someone sighs over a state losing its governor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like a political leader of the state; it is the first letter of the lament.
explanation.definitionFit: Ohioan is the adjective for things belonging to or from Ohio, one of the American states.

clue.text: Laces in shoes

blocks.note: first meaning: secretly adds alcohol or a drug to a drink
second meaning: running shoes with metal studs

explanation.walkthrough: The surface ties laces into shoes; 'Laces' is the verb for doctoring a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Spikes is both a verb for adding liquor to a drink and a noun for athletes' studded running shoes.

clue.text: A bit screwed back, now enabled again

indicators.note: a bit is a small part, so the letters wanted lie within the words
turning a screw back runs it the other way, so the letters read in reverse

blocks.note: found across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A drill bit screwed back in now works once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' reads as a drill bit; it means a small piece of the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: Anew means afresh or once more, a synonym of again.

clue.text: Strike in Asia, case of those in Pakistani city not finishing work

indicators.note: not finishing means the final letter of the city is missing
the case of a word is its outside, so only its outer letters count
in places one piece inside the city

blocks.note: Pakistan's largest city
first and last letters
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A strike in Asia affecting those in a Pakistani city who did not finish work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but it means a blow; 'in Asia' belongs to the definition, since the martial art comes from Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: A karate chop is a hand strike from the martial art that originated in Okinawa, Japan.

clue.text: Vacuous aimless function in meeting place?

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word's insides are removed leaving its outer letters

blocks.note: first and last letters
cot, short for cotangent, a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A pointless, empty social function held at a meeting place.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is an English racecourse; a race meeting is held there.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is the Berkshire racecourse where race meetings such as Royal Ascot take place.

clue.text: Holiday notes for business

blocks.note: first meaning: the music sung by Billie Holiday
second meaning: stuff or palaver

explanation.walkthrough: 'Holiday' reads as a vacation; it is the singer Billie Holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Billie Holiday was a celebrated jazz singer, and the idiom 'all that jazz' uses the word for such stuff or business.

clue.text: Unbending line bending when given little jerk

indicators.note: bending twists something out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder
as, meaning while or when
a tic is a small involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A rigid line flexes when it is given a slight tug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unbending' and 'bending' sit side by side: the first is the definition, the second the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inelastic does not stretch or flex, so it is rigid and unyielding.

clue.text: Firing mechanism on gun initially for pistol

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter only

blocks.note: first letter
the lock is the firing mechanism of a gun

explanation.surface: A gun's firing mechanism, meant for a pistol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' puts G before LOCK in a down-clue sense: G sits on top of LOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Glock is an Austrian brand of semi-automatic handgun, so a pistol.

clue.text: Laid-back figure, one chilled surfer!

indicators.note: laid back means set down backwards, so the number is read the other way

blocks.note: a number
Roman numeral
zen means calm and relaxed

explanation.surface: A relaxed character, a cool dude who rides the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: The surfer here browses the web, not the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: A netizen is a regular internet user, someone who surfs the web.

clue.text: News items though hot replaced by the papers?

indicators.note: replaced by says one letter is swapped out for another piece

blocks.note: items are things
H for hot, as on a tap
identity papers

explanation.surface: News stories, though hot, are taken over by the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The papers' suggests the press; it is identity papers, ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is an old-fashioned word for news or information.
